reason: The cited evidence does not address grain size effects, oxide film formation along grain boundaries, or dislocation pinning in FeNiCrCoCu. E1 reports wear and friction for different coatings but not grain refinement; E2 is a computational study of mechanical properties without wear or oxide data; E3 concerns a different alloy system (FeCoCrNiAlWx) and does not link grain size to oxide stability. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior support.
premises: Grain refinement in FeNiCrCoCu promotes a continuous protective oxide layer along grain boundaries during high-temperature sliding.
This oxide film pins dislocations and restricts localized plastic deformation.
A fine-grained microstructure yields more uniform and continuous oxide coverage than a coarse-grained one.
Improved oxide coverage reduces wear rate and friction coefficient under high-temperature sliding.
The mechanism is dominant under oxidative, high-temperature conditions and less so in inert or low-temperature environments.
